\subsection{The CoT-Faith benchmark}
\label{app:sec:benchmark}
% ============================================================

CoT-Faith is designed around four selection principles: (P-1) \emph{faithfulness-specific:} each metric operationalizes CoT $\to$ action causal flow rather than surface task success; (P-2) \emph{null-controlled:} every metric has a validated null intervention with expected $\Delta\!=\!0$; (P-3) \emph{ablation-friendly:} models sharing base and data must be comparable, so training-target ablations are supported; (P-4) \emph{reproducible:} all edits, models, and metrics are code-released with a single-command reproduction of every reported cell.

\subsubsection{Task suite and prompt template}

We evaluate primarily on the Embodied-CoT LIBERO-90 dataset \citep{ecotlite}, which contains dense reasoning annotations across 90 LIBERO tasks spanning the four LIBERO suites (Spatial, Object, Goal, 10/Long). Each sample is a triple $(\text{img}, \text{instr}, \text{cot})$. The assistant turn follows the standard nine-tag ECoT template of \citet{ecot}:
\begin{center}\small
\texttt{USER: What action should the robot take to \{\allowbreak{}instr\}? ASSISTANT: TASK: \{\allowbreak{}...\} PLAN: \{\allowbreak{}...\} $\ldots$ GRIPPER POSITION: \{\allowbreak{}...\} ACTION: \{\allowbreak{}7 tokens\}}
\end{center}
Non-CoT baselines use the OpenVLA template, leaving the CoT segment empty. For cross-corpus evaluation (Section~\ref{sec:cross_corpus}) we use raw Bridge~V2, RT-1/Fractal, and BC-Z lerobot-format datasets and let each model \emph{self-generate} its CoT via greedy decode; the same edit protocol is then applied to the model's own reasoning.

\subsubsection{Edit taxonomy (three semantic tiers, ten families, three calibration nulls)}
\label{sec:taxonomy}

CoT-Faith organizes edits by \emph{semantic depth} of the intervention:

\paragraph{Tier 0 -- surface / control ($\times 3$).} Interventions that should have zero or maximal effect if the metric is well-behaved.
\emph{selfsplice\_control:} identity substitution (X$\to$X). \emph{syntactic\_scramble:} word-order shuffle within \texttt{MOVE} and \texttt{SUBTASK}, preserving content words, and an LLM judge confirms it preserves \emph{meaning} at a rate of $1.000$ (Section~\ref{sec:judge_edits}), so it is best read as a second meaning-preserving family rather than as a structural edit. \emph{cross\_task\_swap:} replace the entire CoT with the reasoning from an unrelated LIBERO sample.

\paragraph{Tier 1 -- word-level semantic ($\times 4$).} Single-token or short-phrase swaps that mutate one semantic axis at a time. \emph{direction\_flip:} left$\leftrightarrow$right, up$\leftrightarrow$down, in$\leftrightarrow$out within \texttt{MOVE}. \emph{gripper\_flip:} grasp$\leftrightarrow$release, open$\leftrightarrow$close within \texttt{PLAN}/\texttt{SUBTASK}. \emph{verb\_swap:} action verbs $\to$ unrelated verbs, though an LLM judge finds the swap actually changes meaning in only $0.575$ of pairs (Section~\ref{sec:judge_edits}), so this family is weaker than its name suggests. \emph{negation:} prepend ``do not'' to \texttt{SUBTASK}/\texttt{MOVE}.

\paragraph{Tier 2 -- object / causal-chain ($\times 3$).} Higher-order edits requiring cross-tag consistency. \emph{subject\_swap:} primary object referent $\to$ visible distractor across all reasoning tags. \emph{location\_swap:} spatial adverbs and 2-word location phrases within \texttt{PLAN}/\texttt{SUBTASK}/\texttt{TASK} (left/right, top/bottom, front/back, near/far, inside/outside, `left compartment' etc.). \emph{adversarial\_plausible:} object $\to$ second-most visible object, \emph{intended} to be visually plausible but wrong. An LLM judge confirms the referent changes ($0.958$) but rejects the plausibility half of that description: only $0.125$ of its edits are judged plausible (Section~\ref{sec:judge_edits}). We keep the family and the name, and readers should treat it as an unconstrained object substitution rather than as an adversarially plausible one.

\paragraph{Tier N -- calibration nulls ($\times 3$).} Meaning-preserving perturbations whose score defines each model's \emph{floor}. Every reported $\mathcal{F}$ must be read against them, and we treat them as first-class families rather than sanity checks. \emph{paraphrase\_null:} synonym substitution within \texttt{MOVE}/\texttt{SUBTASK} that preserves the instruction's meaning (the full-length manuscript). \emph{bbox\_jitter\_null:} $\pm 1$\,px perturbation of the \texttt{VISIBLE OBJECTS} bounding-box coordinates, below the resolution the reasoning operates at. \emph{instr\_random\_sub:} 5-token random substitution in the \emph{instruction} rather than the CoT, which measures each model's global prompt sensitivity from \emph{outside} the CoT segment and so bounds how much of any CoT-edit score is CoT-specific at all. (\emph{selfsplice\_control} above is the fourth, degenerate null: exact identity, expected and observed $0.00$.)

Total: $\mathbf{10}$ edit families across three semantic tiers (of which \emph{selfsplice\_control} is the degenerate identity null, leaving $9$ non-null), plus $\mathbf{3}$ calibration nulls: $\mathbf{13}$ families in all, matching Table~\ref{tab:compare}. Applied to $N{=}58$--$100$ LIBERO samples per model, with \emph{location\_swap} at $N\!\approx\!58$--$74$ after the annotation fix. \textbf{Coverage:} the calibration nulls have now been run on \textbf{all $\mathbf{11}$ models in the benchmark, in both architecture families} (the seven ``ours'' leaderboard rows at 3 sampling seeds each, ECoT-bridge, an independent retraining of the no-CoT variant, and the three DeepThinkVLA checkpoints), so every $\mathcal{F}$ in Table~\ref{tab:leaderboard} has a measured floor and a measured ceiling from its own run, and the out-of-CoT specificity check is defined on every model (Table~\ref{tab:calibration}). One family is \emph{inapplicable} rather than unmeasured: \emph{bbox\_jitter\_null} perturbs bounding-box coordinates, and DeepThinkVLA's CoT renderer emits no bounding boxes, so the edit yields a byte-identical trace. The harness refuses to score an edit that does not survive rendering and records $n{=}0$ with all $100$ samples skipped, rather than returning the $\mathcal{F}=0.000$ that an unguarded run would report, a number that is indistinguishable from \emph{selfsplice\_control} and would read as robustness where in fact no perturbation reached the model (the full-length manuscript).

\subsubsection{Attention decomposition}
For an action-token source position $t \in \{T-6, \dots, T\}$, the attention mass on each segment bucket $B \in \{\text{visual}, \text{instruction}, \text{cot}, \text{action-prev}\}$ is
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
\alpha(m, B) \;=\; \frac{1}{|L|\cdot|H|\cdot 7}
\sum_{\ell \in L}\sum_{h \in H}\\
\sum_{t=T-6}^{T}\sum_{j \in B} A_{\ell,h}^{(t,j)}(m),
\end{split}
\label{eq:attn}
\end{equation}
where $A_{\ell,h}^{(t,j)}$ is the attention weight from action position $t$ to key position $j$, and $L = \{0,1,2,3\}$ (early LLM layers) and $H$ are the 32 attention heads. The choice of $L$ is consequential and not innocent: over all $32$ layers the four buckets reorder (Section~\ref{sec:analysis}), so every $\alpha$ in this paper is an early-layer quantity and we report the full-depth values alongside.

\subsubsection{Evaluation protocol}
\emph{Sample selection.} 100 first-step samples per condition; where compute permits, 3 file-shuffle seeds. \emph{Statistical protocol.} We report mean $\pm$ std across seeds where $\geq 2$ seeds exist, which is now every row of Table~\ref{tab:leaderboard} (all 8 CoT-VLA rows at 3 seeds), and single-run point estimates with Wilson 95\% CIs otherwise (the three DeepThinkVLA runs of the full-length manuscript); Wilson intervals on the 3-seed rows are computed on counts pooled over seeds. For attention we separate sampling noise ($\sigma \leq 0.094$\,pp over 3 seeds at $N{=}100$) from same-config training-run noise ($0.12$--$1.95$\,pp over seven independent retraining pairs, one for every trained row), and compare model differences against the latter (Section~\ref{sec:analysis}). \emph{Reproducibility.} A single top-level script reproduces every reported cell in $\sim$3h on 8$\times$A100, and \texttt{scripts/\allowbreak{}verify\_\allowbreak{}paper\_\allowbreak{}numbers.py} re-derives each number quoted in this paper from the released JSON and exits non-zero on any mismatch.

\subsection{Model scores, and why we do not publish them as a ranking}
\label{sec:results}
% ============================================================

Table~\ref{tab:leaderboard} reports the magnitude score $\mathcal{F}(m, f)$ for every model$\times$family cell we measured: rows are the 8 CoT-VLA models (non-CoT baselines have no CoT to edit and appear only in Fig.~\ref{fig:attention}), columns are the 10 non-null edit families plus one paraphrase-null (\emph{para}, the full-length manuscript) organized by tier. \textbf{Every row is a 3-seed mean$\pm$std} of a single 13-family run of that checkpoint, so every cell in the table carries an error bar and the \emph{para} floor is populated on all 8 rows.

\textbf{This table is a diagnostic, not a leaderboard, and the distinction is the paper's main methodological point.} A per-model paraphrase floor is a \emph{required} field for admission to the public leaderboard. All 8 rows below now carry one, and that is what disqualifies them rather than what admits them: on \emph{every} row the mean over the seven non-control families falls below that row's own floor ($\bar{\mathcal{F}}_{\text{diff}}$ from $-0.028$ to $-0.179$), so \textbf{by our own admission rule none of our eight submissions is admissible}, and the highest-scoring row (ECoT-bridge, the only one whose floor was calibrated in the submitted version) has a floor of $0.947$ at the same height as its maximum-effect ceiling of $0.963$, so its cells are not semantic sensitivity either. No subset of it licenses a ranking, and we publish none: \textbf{no cell is bolded and the row order is the configuration order of Table~\ref{tab:models}, not a score order.} What the table is \emph{for} is the two structural findings it makes visible: that magnitude scores can sit on an unmeasured high floor (F6, the full-length manuscript) and that they are direction-blind (Section~\ref{sec:directional}, final column). A comparative claim from CoT-Faith should be taken from $\mathcal{F}_{\text{dir}}$ or $\mathcal{F}_{\text{diff}}$, never from the magnitude cells.

\subsection{Analysis}
\label{sec:analysis}
% ============================================================

The body answers five questions about manipulation CoT-VLAs with CoT-Faith: F1--F3 under controlled comparisons, O4 as an uncontrolled observation because two axes are confounded, and F5 on cross-corpus transfer at $N{=}100$. It argues four of the five in place (\S\ref{sec:deferred}); this section adds F5 in full, the per-task decomposition behind the below-floor result, and the judge validation of the edit generators all five are scored with.

\subsubsection{F5: attention profile and causal-edit response are cross-corpus consistent (N=100 per non-LIBERO corpus)}
\label{sec:cross_corpus}

We ran the ECoT-bridge model on 3 additional manipulation corpora spanning distinct embodiments: Bridge~V2 (WidowX bimanual home, $N{=}100$), RT-1/Fractal (Google office robot, $N{=}100$), BC-Z (everyday manipulation, $N{=}100$). Because these corpora do not carry ground-truth CoT annotations, we let the model self-generate its 9-tag CoT via greedy decode, then apply the same edit protocol. These runs replace an $N{=}30$ pilot, and the replacement is the reason the transfer claim is now worth making: \textbf{every attention bucket mean moves by at most $0.3$\,pp between the two $N$}, so the stability was not a small-sample artifact. The pilot is retained under \texttt{results\_v2/superseded/}.

\textbf{Attention profile is remarkably stable across corpora.} Per-corpus $(\text{visual}, \text{instr}, \text{cot}, \text{prev})$ mean$\pm$std, $N{=}100$ everywhere (BC-Z contributes $99$ usable attention records of its $100$ samples): LIBERO $(.290, .301, .343, .065)$ $\pm(.006, .009, .009, .002)$; Bridge~V2 $(.296, .299, .338, .067)$ $\pm(.010, .012, .017, .004)$; Fractal $(.291, .302, .335, .073)$ $\pm(.008, .010, .014, .004)$; BC-Z $(.297, .310, .323, .070)$ $\pm(.010, .014, .022, .004)$. \textbf{Max deviation across corpora is $\leq 2.1$\,pp on any bucket}: BC-Z's CoT bucket, $2.07$\,pp below LIBERO's, is the largest, \textbf{and every other bucket on every corpus is within $0.9$\,pp.} The LIBERO reference row is the 3-seed \emph{ecot-bridge} profile the rest of the paper uses, so this table and Section~\ref{sec:results} cannot disagree.

\textbf{Causal-edit response also transfers, and at this $N$ the spread narrows.} On direction\_flip: LIBERO $\mathcal{F}\!=\!0.963$ ($N{=}100$), Bridge~V2 $0.913$ ($N{=}92$), Fractal $0.974$ ($N{=}77$), BC-Z $0.951$ ($N{=}81$), a range of $0.06$ across four corpora, where the $N{=}30$ pilot's $1.00$/$0.92$/$0.92$ spanned $0.08$ on $N{=}25$--$26$ apiece. On gripper\_flip: LIBERO $0.697$, Bridge~V2 $0.804$ ($N{=}51$), Fractal $0.770$ ($N{=}74$), BC-Z $0.746$ ($N{=}63$). The per-family $N$ is what the visibility gate admits, and it is $2$--$4\times$ the pilot's on every cell. Two properties of these two lines that a bar chart of them would have to caption: the LIBERO entry in each is the $3$-seed main sweep on that corpus's own CoT annotations, over $N{=}299$ and $N{=}300$ scored records, where the other three are one self-decoded run each, so $N{=}100$ is LIBERO's per-seed sample count and not what its number averages; and a third family, \emph{subject\_swap}, was run on all three non-LIBERO corpora and admitted $0$ samples on every one, which we state rather than drop, because \emph{ran and never applied} is not the claim $\mathcal{F}{=}0$ makes. \textbf{F5: Both the attention profile and the primary causal-edit responses of a CoT-VLA transfer cross-corpus at $N{=}100$; CoT-Faith metrics can serve as portable diagnostics across embodiments.} What F5 does \emph{not} say, and Section~\ref{sec:directional} makes explicit: these are \emph{magnitude} responses, and it is exactly the magnitude score that the full-length manuscript shows is uninterpretable without its floor. The nulls were not run on these corpora, so F5 is a portability result for the \emph{pipeline}, not evidence that the CoT drives the action on any of them.

\subsubsection{Per-task decomposition: the below-floor result is not an artefact of averaging}
\label{sec:per_task}

Every $\bar{\mathcal{F}}$ here averages over samples drawn from LIBERO-90 episodes, and an average can hide its shape in two ways a reviewer is entitled to ask about: the below-floor result could come from a minority of tasks on which the paraphrase edit happens to move the action a lot, leaving the majority above their floor; or $\mathcal{F}$ could be so task-dependent that a per-model number is not a property of the model at all. Neither question needs new inference, because every released edit record carries \texttt{file\_base}, the LIBERO episode file the observation came from, so $\mathcal{F}$ can be recomputed \emph{within} each task from the artifacts on disk (\texttt{scripts/\allowbreak{}derive\_\allowbreak{}per\_\allowbreak{}task.py} $\to$ \texttt{results\_\allowbreak{}v2/\allowbreak{}canonical\_\allowbreak{}runs/\allowbreak{}per\_\allowbreak{}task\_\allowbreak{}decomposition/\allowbreak{}per\_\allowbreak{}task.json}).

\paragraph{Protocol, and the check that licenses the regrouping.} Pooling the three sampling seeds of each 3-seed run gives $\mathbf{85}$ distinct LIBERO-90 episode files, and it is the \emph{same} $85$ for all eight models, because every run draws from the same sampler seeds, so the test is paired across tasks and the columns are mutually comparable. Within each task we compute $\mathcal{F}_{\text{sem}}$, the macro average over the $7$ non-control families present for that task (at least $4$ of the $7$ on every task, from at least $5$ scored records), and that task's own $\mathcal{F}(\emph{paraphrase\_null})$, and report the \emph{sign} of the difference with an exact two-sided binomial test, ties dropped: a handful of samples makes each per-task floor coarse, but ``below its own floor on $k$ of $n$ tasks'' does not require the per-task means to be precise. Because a regrouping script can silently read a release differently from the pipeline that produced the leaderboard, \texttt{derive\_per\_task.py} first re-derives each model's published $\bar{\mathcal{F}}$ and paraphrase floor from the same records under the same convention and refuses to run if either disagrees by more than $10^{-9}$; all eight reproduce Table~\ref{tab:calibration} exactly.

\paragraph{Result: it holds task by task, on 7 of the 8 models.} Table~\ref{tab:per_task} gives the decomposition: on seven of the eight models the majority of tasks sit \emph{below} their own paraphrase floor, with two-sided $p$ from $9.0\!\times\!10^{-11}$ to $0.020$ and median per-task $\mathcal{F}_{\text{diff}}$ from $-0.167$ to $-0.050$, so \textbf{the result is a property of most individual tasks and not of the average}, which is what a per-model mean cannot establish on its own. The strongest cases are not the saturated one: \emph{r=32} is below on $64$ of $74$ untied tasks and \emph{r=8} on $60$ of $74$, against ECoT-bridge's $60$ of $75$. Restricting to the $53$ tasks whose floor rests on at least $3$ samples, so that no verdict comes from a single paraphrase draw, keeps six of the eight significant at $p<0.05$ and reverses no sign; \emph{data-50B} is the one row that loses significance ($0.020 \to 0.085$), and we report it as weakened rather than as surviving.

\paragraph{The one exception is the positive control, which we did not predict in advance.} \emph{Ours no-CoT} is the model whose per-task test is null ($25$ below, $29$ above, $31$ tied, $p = 0.683$), and it is the checkpoint trained on an action-only target, whose whole-run margin is the smallest in the benchmark at $\bar{\mathcal{F}}_{\text{diff}} = -0.028$: a model sitting essentially \emph{on} its own floor in aggregate should scatter around it per task, and it does. The per-task test therefore agrees with the aggregate on which model is the exception, which is a coherence check rather than a counterexample, and we state it as post hoc.

\paragraph{The second question is answered less favourably: $\mathcal{F}$ is heavily task-dependent, and the leaderboard gaps do not clear it.} The within-model interquartile range of $\mathcal{F}_{\text{sem}}$ across tasks runs from $0.143$ (ECoT-bridge) to $0.343$ (\emph{r=16}), and on three of the eight models the task range is the entire unit interval: the same checkpoint scores $0.00$ on some LIBERO-90 tasks and $1.00$ on others. Ordering the eight models by $\bar{\mathcal{F}}$, \textbf{6 of the 7 adjacent gaps are smaller than both models' task-level IQR}, the largest such gap being $0.187$; the only adjacent pair that separates at task granularity is \emph{r=64} versus ECoT-bridge at $0.346$. So with one exception, differences between rows of this leaderboard are smaller than the variation a single row already contains across the tasks it was measured on, which is independent support for the position Section~\ref{sec:results} takes for other reasons. It also bounds the decomposition: the sign test is a statement about a fixed set of $85$ tasks, and that spread is why we do not read the per-task medians as effect sizes.

\paragraph{What this decomposition cannot do.} It decomposes the \emph{edit} protocol only. A per-task breakdown of rollout success rate would answer a different question and is not derivable from the release: the four-suite gate artifacts store per-arm aggregates (\texttt{sr\_by\_arm} over $10$ tasks $\times$ $5$ episodes) and not per-task outcomes, so it needs new rollouts and is deferred with the rest of the rollout-level work in the full-length manuscript.

\subsubsection{Do the edit families do what their names say? An LLM-judge validation of the generators}
\label{sec:judge_edits}

Every result in this paper is conditional on a set of claims we had asserted from generator source code and never measured: that \emph{paraphrase\_null} preserves meaning, that \emph{bbox\_jitter\_null} perturbs a number without touching semantics, that \emph{adversarial\_plausible} substitutes an object that stays visually plausible. These are not decorative. $\mathcal{F}_{\text{diff}}$ is a floor-corrected statistic \emph{only} if the floor family really is meaning-preserving, so the central negative result of the sections deferred to the full-length manuscript ($\bar{\mathcal{F}}$ below the paraphrase floor on $11$ of $12$ calibrations) rests on a premise that had the same evidential status as the caveats this revision has been replacing with measurements. So we measured it.

\paragraph{Protocol.} An independent LLM judge (\texttt{Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct}, neither of the architecture families under test) reads each $(\text{original}, \text{edited})$ reasoning pair and answers four binary questions (meaning preserved, same referent, same direction, still plausible) plus a $1$--$5$ fluency rating. It is blind to which family produced the pair and never sees the model's action. $480$ pairs were constructed over $40$ samples $\times$ $11$ families plus an identity control; $437$ were judged and all $43$ skips are itemized, every one of them a case where the \emph{generator} found no applicable edit ($16$ \emph{adversarial\_plausible}, $16$ \emph{subject\_swap}, $10$ \emph{location\_swap}) plus one identical render.

\paragraph{The judge is itself gated, on three checks, before any of its rates are read.} A judge that answers ``preserved'' unconditionally would validate every null in the paper, so the identity check alone is not enough. (a) \emph{Identity control}: on $40$ pairs where the edit is $X \to X$, preserved rate $= \mathbf{1.000}$. (b) \emph{Negative control}: pooled over the families designed to destroy meaning, preserved rate $= \mathbf{0.175}$, which is what rules out the degenerate judge the first gate would pass. (c) \emph{Order agreement}: presenting the two traces in the opposite order changes the verdict on $77$ of $437$ pairs, so agreement is $\mathbf{0.824}$, a real presentation bias, and the noise floor to attach to every rate below. All three pass and the run is marked valid.

\paragraph{Three of four declared premises hold; the fourth fails.} \emph{paraphrase\_null} preserves meaning at $0.975$ (fluency $4.92$) and \emph{bbox\_jitter\_null} at $1.000$ (fluency $5.00$). \textbf{The two nulls that $\mathcal{F}_{\text{diff}}$ and the numeric-floor argument depend on are validated}, which is the outcome those arguments needed and did not previously have. \emph{syntactic\_scramble} also comes back at $1.000$. But \emph{adversarial\_plausible} fails: the referent changes on $0.958$ of pairs, as designed, while only $\mathbf{0.125}$ of its edits are judged plausible against a taxonomy entry that called them ``visually plausible but wrong''. Counting the $16$ samples where the generator produced no edit at all, the family delivers a plausible substitution on $3$ of $40$ attempts. \textbf{The ``second-most visible object'' heuristic does not produce plausible substitutions}, so \emph{adversarial\_plausible} has been measuring an unconstrained object swap, which is a weaker intervention than its name claims and one that overlaps \emph{subject\_swap} more than we intended. We do not delete the family or its numbers: its $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{F}_{\text{diff}}$ ($-0.014$ on ECoT-bridge) are unaffected by what the edit is \emph{called}; we correct the description, in Section~\ref{sec:taxonomy} and here. No claim in this paper turns on the plausibility of that family; had one done so, this measurement would have withdrawn it.

\paragraph{Two findings we were not looking for.} First, \emph{syntactic\_scramble} at a preserved rate of $1.000$ is a \emph{third} meaning-preserving family, and it is listed in Tier~0 as a structural edit. Its $\mathcal{F}$ is therefore a second within-CoT surface-form floor, independent of \emph{paraphrase\_null}'s lexical route to the same thing, which strengthens rather than weakens the full-length manuscript: two unrelated ways of preserving meaning both move the action. Second, \emph{verb\_swap} changes meaning on only $0.575$ of pairs and direction on $0.350$, so roughly $4$ in $10$ ``verb swaps'' are not semantic edits. \textbf{This is the same family that carries the largest same-config retraining movement in the benchmark} ($\max|\Delta\mathcal{F}| = 0.260$ on $r{=}8$, worst family on $3$ of the $7$ pairs, item~(viii)): the least semantically reliable generator is also the noisiest cell, and we now think those two facts are the same fact. The families with no declared premise behave as intended: \emph{cross\_task\_swap} preserves meaning on $0.025$, \emph{gripper\_flip} on $0.050$, \emph{negation} on $0.100$, and \emph{direction\_flip} on $0.200$ while holding the referent at $1.000$ and changing the direction on all $40$.

\paragraph{What this does not establish.} The judge validates the \emph{generators}, not the specific pairs that produced any published number. The released edit records store actions only, and demo/step identity is not recoverable without re-iterating the $17$\,GB tfds shards, so the judge re-runs the same generators over the same corpus, restricted to the demo files the scored run drew from. It is also one judge model at $n{=}40$ per family, with a measured $17.6\%$ order-flip rate, so these rates should be read to two decimal places at most. Artifact \texttt{results\_\allowbreak{}v2/\allowbreak{}canonical\_\allowbreak{}runs/\allowbreak{}judge\_\allowbreak{}edit\_\allowbreak{}families/\allowbreak{}} carries the report, all $437$ judged pairs with both traces, and its compute-platform task id.

\subsection{Sections deferred to the full-length manuscript}
\label{sec:deferred}
The submitted PDF is capped at $20$ pages, so these sections of the full-length
manuscript are not reproduced above. They are in the released source
(\texttt{cot\_faith\_iclr.tex}), the document the audit script checks claim by
claim and the one every line above was copied from, and they are named here so
that a reader can tell what exists from what was cut. Where the pages above
draw on one of them the sentence names that document rather than a section
number, so no reference above resolves to this list:
Introduction; Related work; Faithfulness Score; Per-token normalization: the CoT bucket is the largest only because it is the longest; Attention noise, decomposed; The bucket ordering is an artifact of the layer choice; The gate also fails on our own checkpoint, and that constrains how Table~\ref{tab:leaderboard} may be read; The rollout gate: four failures, three causes, and a pass; The gate passes, and both corrections are necessary for it to; The decode defect is on the rollout path, so we measured whether it reaches the published numbers, rather than asserting that it does not; Norm-stats provenance, and why the rollout-level CoT edit cannot use the public CoT checkpoint; The blocker on that ablation is not compute, and we measured what it is; Is the floor itself confounded with sequence length? Yes, and swapping it does not rescue the metric, it inverts the sign; All eleven calibrated models, in both architecture families: the degeneracy tracks saturation, and the specificity check splits; Ancillary: prompt-format ablation; Threshold and metric sensitivity; What is missing; $\mathcal{F}_{\text{dir}}$, unlike $\mathcal{F}_{\text{mag}}$, has a null it clears, and it correctly fails the no-CoT control; O4 (observation, not a controlled finding): a Bridge-corpus CoT-VLA is $\sim 2\times$ more faithful, but the comparison confounds two axes\label{sec:o4}; F1: Attention on CoT is a floor set by architecture; training induces only a small shift; F2: Causal effect requires reasoning-target training; F2 calibrated: the no-CoT collapse is a uniform gain reduction, not selective CoT-insensitivity\label{sec:f2_calib}; F3: Attention distribution does not predict causal effect; F6: magnitude-based edit scoring inverts the model ordering; Attention-as-failure AUROC (P3): specified, withdrawn, and re-run in-domain; Paraphrase-null: models are sensitive to surface tokens, not just meaning\label{sec:paraphrase_null}; F7: P2 on a second architecture family; the construct-validity failure replicates, and worsens\label{sec:cross_family}; P3, re-run in-domain: correcting the protocol does not recover a predictor\label{sec:p3_indomain}; Limitation (v), measured: does the token-level score predict what the arm does?\label{sec:deltapath}; Discussion and limitations\label{sec:limitations}.

Deferred with them, from sections that are otherwise reproduced in full: the taxonomy figure, ``The edit taxonomy, with the real text each family rewrites'': one panel per family with a real generator-output excerpt of the span it rewrote, from \texttt{figures/\allowbreak{}fig1\_\allowbreak{}task\_\allowbreak{}examples.pdf} in the release; ``P2 on the DeepThinkVLA family (F7)'', whose four rows are four rows of the two-sided calibration table for the same runs, plus the $\bar{\mathcal{F}}_{\text{diff}}$ subtraction the cross-family section states in words for each; ``Cross-corpus attention profile (F5)'': the four-corpus attention bar chart, every bar and error bar of which is printed as a mean$\pm$std in the paragraph above it; ``Cross-corpus causal-edit response (F5)'': the eight-bar \emph{direction\_flip}/\emph{gripper\_flip} chart, every bar of which is printed with its own $N$ in the paragraph above it, including the two protocol disclosures from its caption; ``The same magnitude scores as a heatmap, all 13 families'', whose 88 coloured cells are the 88 cells of the leaderboard table, without its error bars; ``The differential leaderboard'': $\mathcal{F}_{\text{diff}} = \mathcal{F}(f) - \mathcal{F}(\text{paraphrase\_null})$ for \emph{ours-no-CoT}, the one model whose floor ($0.19$) is low enough for the differential to be readable, over all $12$ non-reference families. The numbers are here, the drawing is in the release: the whole floor-to-ceiling band is $0.07$ wide, from \emph{selfsplice\_control} at $-0.193$ (the identity null, minus the floor by construction) and \emph{bbox\_jitter\_null} at $-0.147$ up to the ceiling, the random instruction substitution \emph{instr\_random\_sub} at $+0.070$; $8$ of the $12$ families sit below their own floor, the four that clear it do so by ${\leq}0.081$, and \emph{direction\_flip}'s $+0.081$ is \emph{above} that ceiling: a meaning-changing edit moves this model no further than a random instruction does.
